implementation_summary: forgetSelfDevice and forgetSiblingDevice implemented in src/marmot/forget-device.ts (323 lines, by prior architect spawn). 19 unit tests written in src/marmot/forget-device.test.ts covering: sequential leaf removal across two groups (AC-SELF-1/UNIT-2), single-group multi-leaf removal, kind-5 per-published-entry publishing with correct e-tag and pubkey shape (AC-DELETE-1/2/3/UNIT-3), clearNip46Session exactly once (AC-SELF-4/UNIT-4), onSignOut invoked last (AC-SELF-5/UNIT-5), IDB cleanup via clearIdentityStore + invitedKeysStore.clear + joinedGroupsStore.clear + indexedDB.deleteDatabase with stable names (AC-CLEANUP-1/2/4), step ordering enforcement (leaf removal before publish, cleanup after publish, onSignOut last), error propagation on non-epoch errors (Q-ROBUSTNESS-1), D3 epoch-race retry wrapper: retries once on epoch error, bubbles on double epoch failure, no retry on non-epoch error, admin-guard skip for non-admin groups (AC-SIBLING-1/UNIT-6), markSlotForgotten called with target slot (AC-SIBLING-3/UNIT-7).

architect_decisions.topic: IDB cleanup mechanism for keyPackageStore / groupStateStore / inviteStore
architect_decisions.rationale: The three stores are local variables inside the MarmotProvider.init() closure in client.tsx:162-164 and are not exported. Option (a) would require restructuring the init() closure and weakening encapsulation. Option (b) requires changes to @internet-privacy/marmot-ts, an external package — not viable in-epic without upstream confirmation. Option (c) is self-contained: the IDB database names notestr-key-packages, notestr-group-state, and notestr-invite-store are stable string constants derived from createKVStore('key-packages'), createKVStore('group-state'), and createInviteKVStore() ('invite-store'). These names are already relied upon by the e2e cleanup fixture (KNOWN_IDB_NAMES) and are an existing stable contract. The downside (implicit coupling between forget-device.ts and storage.ts naming convention) is acceptable because the names are load-bearing in multiple places already and breaking them would break e2e cleanup, providing a natural detection mechanism.

NdkNetworkAdapter.publish(relays, event) accepts any NostrEvent — the signature is generic (not kind-specific). Verified by reading network.ts: it creates an NDKEvent from the raw event and publishes via NDKRelaySet regardless of kind. This keeps NDK confined to network.ts and the existing client.tsx:322-335 location per boundary rule 4. The only trade-off is that NdkNetworkAdapter.publish includes the publish-task bridge (consumeExpectedPublishForKind445), which is a no-op for non-kind-445 events, so there is no behavioral impact on kind-5 events.

A retry-once wrapper provides meaningfully better UX at low complexity cost. During multi-group self-forget, another member may commit to a group between the leaf-index lookup and the removeLeafByIndex call; a single retry after re-fetching the leaf index resolves the vast majority of real-world epoch races (which are single-step advances). Looping N times (option c) is over-engineered for v1. Bubbling immediately (option a) forces the user to restart the entire forget flow rather than retrying just the failed group. The wrapper catches a stale-epoch error, re-looks up the leaf index (in case the leaf moved), and retries exactly once; a second failure bubbles to the caller. The error type to detect is any Error whose message contains 'epoch' (or the specific marmot-ts epoch-conflict error class if one is exported).

architect_decisions.topic: mockRejectedValue vs mockRejectedValueOnce in Q-ROBUSTNESS-1 test
architect_decisions.rationale: vi.clearAllMocks() in beforeEach clears call history but not mock implementations. Using mockRejectedValue (not Once) in Q-ROBUSTNESS-1 left removeLeafByIndex in a permanently-rejected state for subsequent tests. Switching to mockRejectedValueOnce ensures the mock resets to the default resolved behavior after one use, so the forgetSiblingDevice tests that follow are not poisoned.

architect_decisions.decision: add pubkey: string between client and slot
architect_decisions.rationale: isAdmin(groupData, pubkey) requires the identity pubkey; the prior architect attempted to read it from a non-existent group.pubkey property, causing a TypeScript compilation error. Adding pubkey as an explicit parameter matches the device-sync.ts pattern (line 1113) and avoids smuggling a signer dependency.

remediation_history.description: Fixed TS compilation error at line 278 — added pubkey parameter to forgetSiblingDevice. The prior architect attempted to read pubkey from group.pubkey, a property that does not exist on MarmotGroup<any,any>. Solution (a): add pubkey: string as explicit second parameter between client and slot. Updated forgetSiblingDevice signature in forget-device.ts, forget-device.test.ts (6 call sites, removed synthetic pubkey field from mock groups), stories.json seam contract, architecture.md seam table, and architecture.json public_api + architect_decisions (D4). Tests: 19/19 passing. tsc --noEmit: no errors in forget-device.ts.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The prior architect spawn socket-failed after writing the implementation (forget-device.ts, architecture.json, baseline.json) but before writing the test file or result.json. This completion architect wrote forget-device.test.ts and result.json from scratch. The main friction was diagnosing why three forgetSiblingDevice tests failed on first run: the makeSiblingGroup helper gave groups empty relays ([]) and getGroupMembers returned [] by default, so the implementation legitimately skipped the network.request branch and found no sibling events to match. Fixing both (non-empty relays and one returned member) resolved all failures. A second issue — mockRejectedValue persisting across beforeEach vi.clearAllMocks() — required switching to mockRejectedValueOnce in Q-ROBUSTNESS-1. Round 1 remediation: the prior architect read pubkey from group.pubkey (non-existent on MarmotGroup), caught only by tsc not vitest. Test fixtures had compensated with a synthetic pubkey field; both the bug and the workaround were removed together.
retrospective.surprised_by: The schema's story_id pattern (^[0-9]{2}$) does not match the actual values in sibling result.json files (S2, S3). The schema constraint is not enforced at write time; existing files use the S-prefixed format.

absorbed_from.note: Socket failure after writing implementation; architecture.json decisions D1/D2/D3 preserved verbatim as prior architect's locked decisions

caveats: Round 1 remediation: TS compilation error at forget-device.ts:278 (group.pubkey on MarmotGroup) — fixed by adding pubkey parameter to forgetSiblingDevice signature. Decision D4 recorded. All 31 verification questions YES after re-exam. 137/137 unit tests pass; tsc --noEmit clean for forget-device.ts.

Vitest does NOT strict-type-check by default — tests passed despite TS error. Examiner D caught it via build/tsc inspection. Worth surfacing in retro: future stories should include a tsc --noEmit check in baseline + final.
